The inputs are synthetic; MCP transport, Runtime/Goja and workspace effects in the planned live study are real local execution. Context7 is a separate external-evidence task.

First select the latest record for EACH issue_id over ALL three batches. Compare updated_at (UTC RFC3339 timestamps); for equal timestamps choose lexicographically greatest batch_id, then greatest record_id (ASCII case-sensitive order). Only AFTER this global latest-state selection keep status=open and severity=high or critical. Group by owner, sort owner ascending, and sort issues within each owner by issue_id ascending. Output exactly total_count and owners; each group contains owner,count,issues; each issue contains issue_id,severity,updated_at,batch_id,record_id. Counts derive from the selected issues, no evidence payload.

Turn 1 contains 36 records (12 per batch). Turn 2 preserves the independent same-version snapshot for each route: R015/ISS-003 is updated to closed at 2026-11-06T00:00:00Z; R037/ISS-NEW is appended to batch-c (37 records total). The old open critical R003 must not survive filtering before deduplication. Timestamp ties for ISS-004 choose batch-b/R016; ties within batch-c for ISS-007 choose R036. Oracles follow these rules; route prompts and tool schemas are identical apart from native/JS entry guidance.
